source_text: Empirical reviews highlight that claimed preventive benefits, such as lowered urinary tract infection rates (occurring in under 1% of uncircumcised infants), do not ethically warrant universal application in low-prevalence settings, as less invasive alternatives exist and long-term outcomes remain contested. [152]
